title: Crewship panel payload — status.v1
description: A grid of named things and how each of them is doing. The cheapest useful panel and the one the wake gates are built around: a threshold on this payload — `any(state == "critical") for: 5m` — is what wakes an agent to write its analysis back onto the same page. Pushed by a routine or by a script running inside a crew container. The server attaches the timestamp, the run id and the producer identity; freshness is computed from the timestamp the server stored, never from anything in this document.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference (informational; the server ignores it). Present so a hand-written payload gets inline validation in an editor while a producer script is being developed.

items.description: The rows of the grid, in the order they should be rendered — the producer decides the order, because only the producer knows whether these are services, machines or months. An empty array is a valid measured answer ("nothing matched") and renders the panel's empty-state sentence; it is not the same as never having pushed, which renders an em dash.

StatusItem.description: One thing being watched. There is no icon, image or link field, and that is deliberate rather than an omission: agent-authored content may not carry URLs or images at all, because both have been used to exfiltrate private data out of a rendered panel through a host the reader trusted.

name.description: What is being watched, in the words the reader will act on ("api", "nightly backup", "Sklad Brno"). Written in the workspace's language by the producing agent; nothing is translated at render time.

state.description: How it is doing. A closed set of three, because the renderer maps each one to a glyph AND a word — state is never carried by colour alone, and these colours are reserved so they can never also mean "series 3".

label.description: The short detail rendered next to the state ("200 OK", "14 min behind", "disk 91 %"). Plain text: no markup, no URL, no entity reference. Omit it when the state is the whole story.
